page: UpCloud PREMIUM-32xCPU-64GB is a compute-oriented server instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9575F processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with a single thread per core, operating at a base speed of 2.0 GHz on a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 400 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address under KVM virtualization.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong compute capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance placing in the top 10% and multi-core performance in the top 25%. The processor's support for advanced vector extensions and cryptography instructions supports its strong Passmark CPU extended instructions and encryption scores, both ranking in the top 25%. However, a notable hardware tradeoff is observed in memory performance; while memory bandwidth for large block reads is strong at 230.25 GB/sec, the overall Passmark memory score falls into the bottom 25%, indicating potential bottlenecks for memory-bound operations.

This instance is suited for compute-heavy workloads such as ray tracing, software compilation, and text decompression, as demonstrated by its top 25% Geekbench ray tracing score and top 10% single-threaded bzip3 decompression performance. It also supports database operations and key-value stores, achieving 67.63 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. Given its high core count relative to memory capacity, the server offers qualitative cost efficiency for parallel processing tasks that do not require massive RAM footprints, making it a viable option for batch processing, web serving, and lightweight LLM text generation.
description: The UpCloud PREMIUM-32xCPU-64GB is an x86_64 compute-focused server featuring 32 AMD EPYC 9575F physical cores on a shared CPU allocation, paired with 64.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 400 GB SSD. Operating under KVM virtualization, this instance delivers top-tier single-core CPU performance and strong multi-core capabilities. While memory bandwidth for large block reads is strong at 230.25 GB/sec, the overall Passmark memory score ranks in the bottom 25%, representing a key hardware tradeoff. The server is highly capable in cryptography, ray tracing, and database operations, as evidenced by its top 25% scores in Passmark database tests and Redis SET operations. It is best suited for compute-intensive workloads, software compilation, and parallel batch processing where CPU performance is prioritized over massive memory capacity.
